stemBlocks.value: Four congruent-looking shapes are drawn on a square grid. Shape P (shaded) has vertices (3, 6), (4, 7), (6, 7), (6, 8), (7, 8), (7, 6). Shape Q has vertices (7, 6), (8, 6), (8, 7), (10, 7), (11, 8), (7, 8). Shape R has vertices (−5, 8), (−4, 8), (−4, 7), (−2, 7), (−1, 6), (−5, 6). Shape S has vertices (−1, 1), (7, 1), (7, 5), (5, 5), (5, 3), (1, 3). (a) Describe fully the single transformation that maps shape P onto (i) shape Q, (ii) shape R, (iii) shape S. (d) On the grid, draw the image of shape P after a translation by the vector (−2, 3) and label it T.
Think first: Compare sizes first: same size means reflection, rotation or translation; double the size means an enlargement.

stemBlocks.altText: Source visual for edmar-csec-p259-q18 from workbook page 259.

solutionSteps.instruction: Compare P with Q by pairing corresponding vertices.

contentBlocks.value: (3,6) → (−1,6), (4,7) → (−2,7), (6,7) → (−4,7), (6,8) → (−4,8), (7,8) → (−5,8), (7,6) → (−5,6): the y-coordinates are unchanged and each pair of x-coordinates averages 1
Result: Reflection in the line x = 1

solutionSteps.instruction: Compare P with S, checking lengths first.

contentBlocks.value: P is 4 units wide and 2 tall; S is 8 wide and 4 tall, so lengths are doubled — an enlargement of scale factor 2

solutionSteps.instruction: Find the centre of that enlargement using centre = 2 × object − image.

contentBlocks.value: With (3, 6) → (−1, 1): (6 − (−1), 12 − 1) = (7, 11); the same centre works for every vertex, e.g. (7, 8) → (7, 5) gives (7, 11)

solutionSteps.instruction: Translate P by the vector (−2, 3) for shape T.

contentBlocks.value: Subtract 2 from each x and add 3 to each y

strategyBlocks.value: Pair up corresponding vertices of P with each image shape, test the coordinate rule on all six points, and use it to name the transformation and locate its centre or mirror line.

finalAnswerBlocks.value: (a)(i) A rotation of 180° about the point (7, 7) (a half turn, so no direction needs to be stated).  (ii) A reflection in the line x = 1.  (iii) An enlargement of scale factor 2 with centre (7, 11).  (d) Shape T has vertices (1, 9), (2, 10), (4, 10), (4, 11), (5, 11) and (5, 9).

whyThisWorks.value: Comparing lengths separates the transformations that preserve size (rotation, reflection, translation) from an enlargement, which multiplies every length by the scale factor. For a half turn, the centre is the midpoint of every point-and-image pair; for a reflection, the mirror is the perpendicular bisector of those pairs; for an enlargement, the centre is the point where all the lines joining object to image meet, found algebraically from the scale factor.

commonErrors.misconception: Describing the P → Q half turn as a translation because the shape has 'moved across'.
